purpose: The endpoint and storage-prefix halves of G8.5, recorded the way docs/route-divergence.json records the route half. That file answers which routes exist, which verbs they export, which status their redirects emit and which buckets their migrations create. This one answers the two questions nothing asked: does every one of the register's 88 endpoint entries resolve to the contracts it names, and does every storage prefix the register declares describe the buckets and object keys the live code actually addresses. scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts compares every list below in both directions, so an unlisted divergence fails and a listed one that is fixed, moved or no longer reproducible fails too.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. An endpoint whose success contract is undefined has no declared success status or body, and an object key no declared prefix describes has no declared filename contract, retention id or disposition. Each entry names what is missing and what closing it needs.
measured: 2026-09-10, against docs/route-register.json (160 routes: 62 pages, 88 endpoints, 10 redirects; 6 storagePrefixes over 4 buckets), src, worker/src, workers, supabase/migrations and docs/retention.md.

csrfTransportNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5; owner decision "CSRF: build the token everywhere"). The register's csrfTransport stands and is built. src/lib/security/session-csrf-core.ts mints X-Inherit-CSRF as <expiresAt>.<random>.<mac>: a keyed digest of the session kind, the session (the account and its auth session, or the SHA-256 of the rights-session or activation-candidate cookie), the registered route and a twelve-hour expiry, none of which travels in the token. The page or the signed-in shell renders it and stores nothing. The route verifies it against the live request, and public.consume_session_csrf_v1 (20261024220000_session_csrf_tokens.sql, a guarded production release) spends its hash once, refusing a spent token, an expiry beyond the lifetime and an authenticated token whose auth session is no longer live; the response that spends one carries its successor in the same header. A missing, spent, other-session or other-route token is refused before the handler runs: authenticated-mutation-v1's 403 request_forbidden on an authenticated route, the 404 not_found of token-api-v1 or token-candidate-api-v1 on a purpose-session route. Operation nonces are unchanged and separate (operationNonceIsNotCsrf). The 74 routes of SESSION_CSRF_ROUTES require it (37, and api.embryo-acknowledge since the merge with G8.5's form shapes; api.subjects, api.future-person-claimant-bind, api.future-person-correction and api.appeal-complete since 2026-11-19, moved from csrfOwnDesign; fourteen more the same day in stage two, with api.consents and api.subject-drafts now gated on every body; eighteen more in the migration stage, the same day, on five more session kinds that public.consume_session_csrf_v2 spends and holds to their live rows, with api.future-person-claim-objection taking a rights or an account token), with api.embryo-withdraw sharing api.cohort-restrict's token as its policy.aliasOf; src/lib/security/session-csrf-routes.test.ts drives each through its handler, and scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts finds no client request, form or not, that omits the header. auth.sign-out is a scripted form that sends it and checks the exact Origin. No route the register binds keeps an X-Inherit-CSRF of its own design since the migration stage, and no branch either since 2026-11-22: csrfOwnDesign is empty (the owner's decision of that day, "G8.5: the reviewer chunk-acknowledgement address accepts either kind of session": api.claim-review-chunk-acknowledgement takes a reviewer token first and an account token second, the second route SESSION_CSRF_SECOND_KINDS declares, and the TEST account archive's per-chunk proof moved to X-Inherit-Operation-Proof). api.evidence-chunk's value is verified on every chunk and not spent (principle 3). No formRequestDivergence row records a CSRF omission any more.

csrfOwnDesignNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5). Every route the register binds to csrfTransport whose X-Inherit-CSRF is not the one-time session token of src/lib/security/session-csrf.ts, read from its handler: what the header carries, the kind (digest-not-one-time: a keyed digest of the session that a replay can repeat, so the paired one-time nonce or the session's own rotation is what refuses it; operation-token: the one-time operation or presentation value itself, which operationNonceIsNotCsrf says a CSRF value is not; derived-one-time: a distinct value bound to a one-time token; none), and whether it is one-time. branch marks a route whose other bodies use the session token. src/lib/security/session-csrf-routes.test.ts holds this list to the register in both directions, with SESSION_CSRF_ROUTES, and each row to the literal it cites. Moving a row onto the session token is engineering work once the owner says these designs should go; the two upload-session routes also need a carrier for the first token of a session a response opens. 2026-11-19 (G8.5 stage one, the owner's "build the token everywhere"): the four rows that fit without a migration or a design question moved onto the session token and left this list (api.subjects, api.future-person-claimant-bind, api.future-person-correction, api.appeal-complete); each kept its one-time nonce. Of the 34 left after it, 2026-11-19 (G8.5 stage two, under the owner's principles for the CSRF register amendments of the same day): fourteen whole rows and the two branch rows moved onto the session token and left this list (api.account-completion, api.invitations, api.embryo-cohort-drafts, api.legal-evidence-upload-session, api.embryo-record-key-cards-rights, api.export, api.subject-export, api.future-person-export, api.future-person-identity-profile, api.future-person-recovery-key, api.future-person-analysis-stop, api.future-person-delete, api.appeal-document-session, api.third-party-subject-export; api.consents, api.subject-drafts). Each kept its one-time operation value where the register now names it: a body field (presentationToken, artifactPresentationToken, nonce), X-Inherit-Operation-Nonce, or X-Inherit-Operation-Proof for the export routes' sealed proof and the identity profile's derived proof; the two evidence-session openers hand the evidence session's value over in X-Inherit-Evidence-CSRF. The 18 left: 17 need a session kind the consume function does not accept (reviewer, upload-session, claim-session, evidence-session, reset-session), so a migration; api.future-person-claim-objection needs the gate to accept two session kinds for one route (the rights session for its link branch and the account session for its registered accountEquivalent branch), which the owner's principles do not settle. 2026-11-19 (G8.5, the migration stage, under the same principles and the owner's decision of the same day "G8.5: the claim-objection address accepts either kind of session"): all 18 whole rows moved onto the session token and left this list. The seventeen that needed a session kind the consume function did not accept are spent by public.consume_session_csrf_v2 (20261119120000_session_csrf_purpose_kinds.sql, a guarded production release), which holds each kind to its live row: reviewer (api.legal-evidence-review, api.appeal-review, api.future-person-documentary-verification, api.future-person-claim-review, api.future-person-claim-release, api.future-person-claim-objection-review, api.future-person-correction-review, api.claim-review-receipt, api.claim-review-chunk-acknowledgement), upload-session (api.embryo-ingest-configure, api.embryo-ingest-mapping, api.embryo-ingest-complete), claim-session (api.future-person-claim-document-session, api.future-person-claim-complete), evidence-session (api.evidence-chunk, api.evidence-complete) and reset-session (auth.reset-password-submit). api.future-person-claim-objection takes a rights token first and an account token second (SESSION_CSRF_SECOND_KINDS, the only route that declares one). Each kept its one-time value where it was (the review, receipt, acknowledgement, claim, completion, mapping and objection nonces in their bodies), except api.embryo-ingest-complete's ingest_complete_csrf operation token, which moved to X-Inherit-Operation-Nonce. The review pages render the reviewer's tokens and the case GETs return none; an opening answer hands over the opened session's first tokens in X-Inherit-Evidence-CSRF or X-Inherit-Upload-CSRF; the reset callback puts the reset session's first token in its Lax cookie; api.evidence-chunk keeps one session-bound value for the chunk stream (principle 3). One branch row stays: the TEST account archive's acknowledgement on api.claim-review-chunk-acknowledgement's path keeps its own per-chunk value. 2026-11-22 (G8.5, the owner's decision of the same day "G8.5: the reviewer chunk-acknowledgement address accepts either kind of session"): the last branch row left this list. api.claim-review-chunk-acknowledgement checks the signed-in reviewer's one-time token first and the signed-in account's second (SESSION_CSRF_SECOND_KINDS, which now declares this route beside api.future-person-claim-objection, and withReviewerOrAccountCsrf), spends whichever it finds and runs only that principal's branch. The TEST account archive's per-chunk acknowledgement proof is unchanged and checked as before; under principle 2 it travels in X-Inherit-Operation-Proof both ways (the chunk's GET answer hands it over, the acknowledgement sends it back), where X-Inherit-CSRF carried it. The acknowledgements of one download go one after another, so each spends a one-time account token and carries the previous answer's successor; like the reviewer's, they are not a chunk stream (principle 3 names uploads). The settings data page renders that account token only while the TEST archive delivery is on. No migration: consume_session_csrf_v1 spends the account token as it spends every authenticated one. This list now has no row.
endpointResponseDivergenceNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5). A registered endpoint whose method matches the register but whose answer does not. Each row names the register text it departs from and literal evidence in the code that produces the answer; scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts checks both, and src/app/api/export/route.test.ts drives the cookieless GET itself, so the row fails as stale the day the behaviour or the register changes. api.export is the case docs/route-divergence.json#methodDivergenceNote describes since 1 October: verb correspondence only. 2026-10-24 (D-103 and G8.5's "code to the register"): api.subject-drafts' Path A answer joins them. The register's subject-draft-created-v1 (201) and reserved draft wait on a product decision, because the draft's next step is an uploader artifact that Path A's inviter, who never holds the file, cannot truthfully sign; the row says which two decisions would close it. 2026-11-19, owner decision ("G8.5: Path A's invitation stays one step"): the register describes what the route does on Path A. api.subject-drafts' policy.pathAOneStepInvitation reserves the draft and creates the invitation and its mail in one transaction, with no inviter artifact, and answers path-a-invitation-created-v1 (202 { accepted: true }, bound to the route as policy.pathASuccessResponseContract); api.invitations no longer takes a Path A draft. Path B keeps subject-draft-created-v1 and the uploader artifact. The Path A row closes and is removed; the two api.export rows remain.

endpointResponseDivergence.registered: methodRequestContracts.GET.missingPrincipalBoundExportCookie is resource-not-found-v1 (404 JSON), and methodPolicies.GET is poll-status-only with zero enqueue, session, cookie, credential or other write side effects.
endpointResponseDivergence.built: 200 application/zip: the synchronous account archive, streamed by the original GET for any signed-in request without the __Host-inherit-export cookie, the request /settings/data's export link makes. Signed out it answers 401 text/plain, and a failed read 503 text/plain.
endpointResponseDivergence.why: The register describes only the asynchronous large-export contract (G5.6, owner decision 2026-09-25). The synchronous GET is the export people actually use today: the cookie-present GET and the POST exist since 1 October, but the POST cannot create an archive (next row), so retiring the synchronous GET now would leave no working export, which G5.6 forbids. docs/account-archive-orchestration.md records it as kept "unchanged for compatibility".
endpointResponseDivergence.closing: Owner, then engineering: the export provider and delivery choice (docs/register-divergence-proposals.md: "The export storage/delivery proposal is awaiting the owner's answer"); then the complete asynchronous transition retires the synchronous GET, this row goes stale and src/app/api/export/route.test.ts's register check is updated with it.

endpointResponseDivergence.registered: operation create enqueues and answers large-export-delivery-v1.pending (202); open-ready creates a download session. No response contract bound to api.export declares a 503.
endpointResponseDivergence.built: 503 {"error":"unavailable"} for create, after the CSRF and nonce checks, because approvedAccountArchiveGeneration() returns null; open-ready answers 404 while no export is ready, and would answer the same 503 if one were, because no delivery capability is configured.
endpointResponseDivergence.why: The POST is built closed on purpose until a provider is approved (docs/account-archive-orchestration.md: "the export provider remains an unanswered owner choice. The actual POST refuses before durable create"), and no public page offers it. Its refusal is a status the register does not let the route answer.
endpointResponseDivergence.closing: Owner: the same provider decision. Until then either the register binds a closed-capability response to api.export, or the door answers a bound contract, as the other routes built closed do with resource-not-found-v1 (engineering, once the owner picks).

The decision says any kind that turns out to have no way to be withdrawn comes back to the owner and the amendment does not paper over it. api.consent-revoke's policy.withdrawalRoutes.cases names the routes that withdraw all eleven dispositionCases kinds (donor attribution as a consent that cannot be given yet; self-upload-class-consent since the owner decision of 2026-11-19, "Withdrawing consent for a person's own DNA file deletes the files and all made from them"; other-adult-uploader-consent.upload-other-adult since the owner decision of 2026-11-19, "An uploader's withdrawal for another adult's file deletes it, unless that adult holds the record themselves", for a record whose adult holds no account of their own on it, the own-account branch waiting on the owner; and embryo-nonparent-uploader-own-upload-artifact since the owner decision of 2026-11-19, "A non-parent uploader's withdrawal for an embryo upload stops analysis and deletes, as they signed"). Listing a kind records it; it does not bless it.
